newsitem.title: USA: Natgas futures pare gains late but still finish up.
newsitem.headline: Natgas futures pare gains late but still finish up.

text.p: NYMEX front-month Henry Hub natgas futures finished mostly higher Wednesday despite some sharp gains this morning, supported by firm cash prices, industry sources said.

October settled 1.5 cents stronger at $1.806 per million British thermal units after reaching a high of $1.85 earlier. November finished down one cent after holding a four-cent lead earlier in the session.
"There's no weather in the forecast. The only demand we're seeing is storage," said one trader, adding that he saw the firm cash as the main force driving the market higher today.
"From this point, I think everything is riding on the AGAs (American Gas Association data) right now," the trader added.
Traders said earlier today that they expected a build between 83 and 93 billion cubic feet (bcf) in tonight's AGA storage report, according to a Reuter poll.
Traders still pegged support in October in the $1.73-1.74 area. Further support was seen at $1.68. Traders said resistance was first in the mid-$1.80s, then in the low-$1.90s and $1.955.
The Oct/Nov spread narrowed by 1.1 cents to 22.4 cents.
In the cash market, prices on the U.S. Gulf Coast pipes moved slightly higher today into the low-$1.80s despite forecasts for cooler weather by the end of the week in the eastern U.S.
NYMEX's October Permian contract ended 1.5 cents higher at $1.53. An estimated four lots exchanged hands.
On the physical side, Permian prices were carried into the mid-to-high $1.60s by the New Mexico outage, gaining more than five cents on the day.

On the KCBT, October also trimmed its gains late to settle only 0.4 cent higher at $1.596 after hitting a high of $1.625 earlier. The East/West spread narrowed by two cents to 21 cents (NYMEX premium).
Physical prices at Waha were also higher in the mid-to-high $1.70s.
